rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s ruling that a prayer without reciting the Opening is deficient, and tells one praying behind an imam to recite it silently to himself.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In the divine report the Opening is divided into halves: praise belongs to God, the central pledge of worship and seeking help is shared, and its closing requests belong to the worshipper, who receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan; Abu Zurʿa says both transmission versions are sound.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن

rows.speaker: وائل بن حجر
rows.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr reports that the Prophet recited the verse’s ending, said amin, and extended his voice on it.
rows.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر، قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tirmidhi says many Companions, Successors, and later scholars, including al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq, hold that a man raises his voice when saying amin rather than hiding it.
rows.anchor: ومن بعدهم يرون أن الرجل يرفع صوته بالتأمين ولا يخفيها

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muḥammad prefers Sufyan’s account: Shuʿba misidentifies Ḥujr, adds ʿAlqama to the chain, and reports a lowered voice where the stronger wording says the Prophet extended it.
rows.anchor: سمعت محمدا يقول حديث سفيان أصح من حديث شعبة في هذا وأخطأ شعبة في مواضع من هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: أبو زرعة
rows.claim: Abu Zurʿa also judges Sufyan’s version more accurate; al-ʿAlāʾ b. Ṣāliḥ transmits a version like Sufyan’s.
rows.anchor: وسألت أبا زرعة عن هذا الحديث فقال حديث سفيان في هذا أصح من حديث شعبة

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report from Wāʾil b. Ḥujr hasan.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى حديث وائل بن حجر حديث حسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the revelation in 2:284 distressed the believers; the Prophet told them to answer that they heard and obeyed, God placed faith in their hearts, and revelation then came down through 2:286.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās’s report, God answers the requests not to punish forgetfulness or error, impose the former peoples’ burden, or demand the unbearable, and to pardon, forgive, and show mercy, with “I have done so.”
rows.anchor: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan and notes another route from Ibn ʿAbbās, as well as a related report from Abū Hurayra.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن وقد روي هذا من غير هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Masruq reports that ʿĀʾisha named three grave lies: that Muhammad saw God (she identifies the figure as Gabriel, seen in his created form only twice), concealed revelation, or knew the unseen; she cites revelation against each claim.
rows.anchor: عِنْدَ عَائِشَةَ فَقَالَتْ يَا أَبَا عَائِشَةَ ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ بِوَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ فَقَدْ أَعْظَمَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْفِرْيَةَ

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن صحيح

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada describes the poor Banu Ubayriq household and says Bashir was a hypocritical poet who composed satire against the Prophet’s Companions and passed it off as others’ work.
rows.anchor: قتادة بن النعمان قال كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق بشر وبشير ومبشر وكان بشير رجلا منافقا يقول الشعر يهجو به أصحاب رسول

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Rifaʿa b. Zayd’s store was broken into and food and weapons stolen; the household was suspected, while its members blamed Labid, a righteous Muslim, and denied the theft.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: After the Prophet rebuked Qatada for accusing a household known for piety without proof, revelation identified Banu Ubayriq as the traitors and ordered judgment by what God revealed rather than advocacy for them.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: The narration explains “seek God’s forgiveness” as concerning what the Prophet had said to Qatada; it then condemns defending those who betray themselves, hiding from God, and falsely accusing Labid.
rows.anchor: مِمَّا قُلْتَ لِقَتَادَةَ ‏:‏ ‏(‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: The account connects God’s favor and mercy with protecting the Prophet from the faction’s attempt to mislead him in the Banu Ubayriq case; the revelation exposed their plot and taught him what he had not known.
rows.anchor: وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet returned the weapons to Rifaʿa; when Rifaʿa dedicated them to God’s path, Qatada recognized that his uncle’s Islam was sound.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة لما أتيت عمي بالسلاح وكان شيخا قد عسى أو عشي في الجاهلية وكنت أرى إسلامه مدخولا

words: وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Bashir fled to the polytheists after the revelation; further verses condemn opposing the Messenger and associating partners with God, and Ḥassān’s satire led Sulafa to cast Bashir’s belongings out.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل القرآن لحق بشير بالمشركين فنزل على سلافة بنت سعد ابن سمية فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb: Muhammad b. Salama alone gives it as a connected report, while Yunus b. Bukayr and others transmit it as mursal without Qatada’s father and grandfather.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث غريب لا نعلم أحدا أسنده غير محمد بن سلمة الحراني

none: The hadith concerns intercession for major sinners and does not cite or interpret 7:11’s account of creation and the prostration to Adam.

words: وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the report Umar transmits, the Prophet explains the verse as God bringing descendants from Adam’s back and assigning one group to Paradise and one to Fire, each doing the deeds of its destination.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ ثُمَّ مَسَحَ ظَهْرَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَاسْتَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ ذُرِّيَّةً

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked what use deeds have if destinies are set, the Prophet says God enables the person destined for Paradise to do its deeds until death, and likewise the person destined for Fire.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ إِذَا خَلَقَ الْعَبْدَ لِلْجَنَّةِ اسْتَعْمَلَهُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ

rows.speaker: أبو عيسى
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan but notes Muslim b. Yasar did not hear directly from Umar; some versions insert an unnamed intermediary.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن

none: The prayer-for-need report mentions a person from among the children of Adam only generically; it does not explain the primordial covenant in 7:172.
The report reassures listeners about the numbers destined for Paradise and Fire; its mention of the children of Adam does not interpret the covenant in 7:172.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Quraysh, prompted by Jews, asked the Prophet about the spirit and 17:85 was revealed; after they claimed the Torah gave them much knowledge, God revealed that the sea would run out before His words.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tirmidhi grades this route hasan sahih gharib.
rows.anchor: قال هذا حديث حسن صحيح غريب من هذا الوجه
